title: Cross-region rollout phasing and standby capacity (Q4 2025)
content:
Goal: Define a phased, low-risk GPU driver upgrade and maintenance window plan across four primary regions (us-west1, us-east1, eu-west1, ap-southeast1) that preserves SLOs and leaves standby capacity for emergency failover. This sheet captures per-region time windows, targeted drain percentages, canary steps, rollback criteria, and communication templates for product and sales teams.

Summary of approach:
- Stagger windows by 48–72 hours between regions to allow measurement and rollback.
- Keep a minimum of 15–25% of regional GPU capacity on warm standby (not drained) during each window for immediate failover.
- Use a 3-phase canary inside each region: micro-canary (1 host), mini-canary (5–10% capacity), bulk drain (to target).
- Pre-warm cross-region routing and validate fallback playbook before draining.
- Automated health checks + manual signoff at each phase transition.

Per-region schedule and capacity plan (UTC):
- us-west1:
  * Window: 2025-11-05 02:00–06:00 UTC (primary maintenance)
  * Target drain: 38% of total GPU slots (125 of 330 GPUs)
  * Standby reserve: 20% (~66 GPUs) kept warm, not drained
  * Canary steps: micro-canary at 02:00 (single host), mini-canary at 02:20 (10% capacity), decision point 02:50 for bulk drain
  * Fallback region: us-east1 (pre-warmed routing capacity + KV cache warmup)

- us-east1:
  * Window: 2025-11-07 04:00–09:00 UTC
  * Target drain: 33% (110 of 335 GPUs)
  * Standby reserve: 18% (~60 GPUs)
  * Canary steps: micro-canary 04:00, mini-canary 04:30, bulk decision 05:00
  * Fallback region: eu-west1 for cross-continental overflow (limited to read-only eval traffic during peak)

- eu-west1:
  * Window: 2025-11-10 01:00–06:00 UTC
  * Target drain: 40% (140 of 350 GPUs)
  * Standby reserve: 25% (~88 GPUs) because of predicted higher steady traffic
  * Canary steps: micro-canary 01:00, mini-canary 01:30, bulk drain 02:15
  * Fallback region: us-east1 (latency > threshold gating)

- ap-southeast1:
  * Window: 2025-11-13 03:00–09:00 UTC
  * Target drain: 30% (90 of 300 GPUs)
  * Standby reserve: 15% (~45 GPUs)
  * Canary steps: micro-canary 03:00, mini-canary 03:40, bulk drain 04:30
  * Fallback region: eu-west1 (capacity constrained during daytime local hours)

Operational playbook (step-by-step):
1) Pre-window (T-72h):
   - Announce maintenance to product, sales, and external status page (draft message in 'communications' section below).
   - Verify: driver package signed, rolling image salted and in registry, kernel compatibility matrix validated for all instance types.
   - Run capacity simulation: synthetic traffic replay to check cold-switch routing and cache warmup times.
   - Confirm on-call roster for SRE, infra, and product liaison.

2) Pre-drain (T-2h):
   - Snapshot metrics baseline (p50/p95 latency, error rate, GPU utilization, queue depth).
   - Create per-region incident channel and runbook pinned.
   - Tag warm standby hosts and mark them as non-drainable in autoscaler config.

3) Micro-canary (start):
   - Evacuate single host, upgrade driver, run smoke generations and eval set (10 prompts).
   - Pass criteria: no increase >2x in error rate and p95 latency delta < 25% vs baseline for 15m.

4) Mini-canary (scale):
   - Drain 5–10% capacity, upgrade, and run throughput tests plus end-to-end app path.
   - Pass criteria: sustained error rate <0.5% and 95th percentile latency within agreed SLO tolerance for 30m.
   - If failure: rollback to previous driver on canary hosts and abort bulk drain.

5) Bulk drain and upgrade:
   - Proceed in 10–15% increments until target drain reached. Manual signoff at each increment.
   - Monitor real-time dashboards (token-level latency, model timeouts, kernel OOM alerts).

6) Post-upgrade validation (T+30m after bulk complete):
   - Run regression set: 200 prompts across high-frequency customers and open-models.
   - Validate routing failover by simulating a cold host failure and ensuring warm standby picks up <60s.

Rollback criteria and thresholds (immediate rollback triggers):
- Sustained p95 latency increase >50% across two consecutive 10m windows.
- Error rate spike to >2% sustained for 10m (customer-visible 5xxs or model timeouts).
- Kernel-level OOMs or CUDA driver crashes on >3% of upgraded hosts.
- Canary-specific instability (flaky initialization) observed during micro- or mini-canary.

Fallback routing plan and capacity math:
- Maintain advertised standby for each region in routing config; ensure cross-region egress limits are increased ahead of maintenance.
- Example: us-west1 standby 20% = 66 GPUs. If bulk drain requires additional 60 GPUs, route 30–40% of excess traffic to us-east1 queue while keeping token-level timeouts increased for affected customers (notify).
- Pre-warm KV cache on fallback hosts for top-50 customers to avoid cold-start quality regressions.

Communication templates (status snippets):
- Pre-window announcement: "Planned maintenance: GPU driver upgrade in us-west1 on 2025-11-05 02:00–06:00 UTC. We expect up to 38% capacity to be drained; standby capacity will remain. No API key changes required. Contact infra-oncall@redwood.ai for urgent questions."
- Incident start: "Maintenance window started for us-west1. Canary underway (1 host). Monitoring for regressions. Status channel: #infra-maintenance-us-west1."
- Recovery/complete: "Maintenance completed for us-west1. All upgraded drivers are healthy. No customer-facing incidents detected. Post-mortem to follow at CONFLUENCE-12345."

Testing and validation matrices to run during each phase:
- Functional: sample prompts + deterministic checks for top 20 models.
- Performance: p50/p95 latencies, tokens/sec, tail latency heatmap across GPUs.
- Reliability: GPU process restarts, driver panics, kernel OOMs.
- Quality: output regression tests against golden prompt set (token diffs threshold per model).

Runbook links and artifacts (quick list):
- Driver packaging checklist: CONFLUENCE-12345
- Automated canary job: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-scripts/actions/upgrade-canary
- Capacity simulation harness: JIRA-INFRA-8702

Owners and on-call assignments:
- Region owner (us-west1): Andre Kim (primary), Priya Rao (backup)
- Region owner (us-east1): Liam O'Sullivan (primary), Maya Chen (backup)
- SRE lead (coord): Sofia Martinez
- Product liaison: Elena Novak

Open risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Cross-region network egress limits might throttle fallback traffic. Mitigation: Pre-request quota increases and schedule bulk drain off business hours for regions with fragile egress.
- Risk: Unexpected model-level regressions after driver change. Mitigation: Hold 10% of capacity un-upgraded for 48h as a quick rollback pool for high-value customers.
- Risk: On-call fatigue during multi-region run. Mitigation: Keep stagger >=48h and cap work windows to 6h per region; use 3-person critical rotation.

Next steps / action items (owners):
- [Maya Chen] Finalize driver package and sign-off checklist by 2025-10-31.
- [Andre Kim] Run top-50 customer cache pre-warm script on fallback hosts by 2025-11-03.
- [SRE] Add automated rollback trigger to deployment pipeline and smoke-run integration by 2025-11-01.
- [Product] Draft customer-facing post-maintenance note and pre-announce to enterprise accounts by 2025-11-02.

Notes and historical context:
- This plan differs from earlier mass-drain approaches by emphasizing small-step canaries, explicit standby percentages, and pre-warmed cross-region fallbacks. Past upgrades where we skipped mini-canary led to localized latency spikes (see postmortem JIRA-INFRA-7401).

Appendix: quick checklist (T-24h, T-2h, T+1h)
- T-24h: Confirm clear communication, ensure backup images, check monitoring alerts baseline.
- T-2h: Lock autoscaler policies, mark standby hosts, pin routing configs.
- T+1h: Confirm metrics stable, unpin standby hosts after 4h stable, schedule post-mortem.

Document history:
- Created: 2025-10-28 by Maya Chen
- Reviewers: Andre Kim, Priya Rao, Liam O'Sullivan
- Last modified: 2026-02-18 (added more conservative rollback thresholds and ap-southeast1 window adjustments)
